<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-defaults/ui.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **4** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **139** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f368b7e980d3df201620098be965523b50d6df19` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `7ea2f37356cdc3787e2053c4786707be157a22a5` — the merge of head `fc3733b9714493610f60cc80e7849f36471a6548` into base `f368b7e980d3df201620098be965523b50d6df19`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 7ea2f37356cdc3787e2053c4786707be157a22a5 && git checkout 7ea2f37356cdc3787e2053c4786707be157a22a5
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin f368b7e980d3df201620098be965523b50d6df19 fc3733b9714493610f60cc80e7849f36471a6548 && git checkout -B drift-repro f368b7e980d3df201620098be965523b50d6df19 && git merge --no-ff fc3733b9714493610f60cc80e7849f36471a6548
```

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `24d9bdcbf008e79365002ffb56616f8d1e4b3b74`
Local-runs: none

Read-only: the card body and its four comments (triage `6093968052`, claim `6094254055`, dev report `6094863892`, ACCEPT `6094884470`), the PR body and file list, the net diff against the merge-base `e22315238f` (9 files, +233 / −7, identical to the three-dot diff against `origin/main`), and the head's check-runs. The branch is at the brief's sha. Nothing built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

- **The default and its `describe`.** `UserActionsConfigSchema.editInline` is `z.boolean().default(true)`; the `describe` says on by default, a user who may update the object edits a cell in place with the field's type-aware widget under the permission gate, and `editInline: false` makes the list read-only in place — the card's three sentences. The schema docblock records the ruling verbatim. Held.
- **`DEFAULT_CHANGES_BY_MAJOR[17]`.** The row is `ui/UserActionsConfig:editInline`, `from: 'false'`, `to: 'true'`, inside the `17: [` block (lines 218–621 at head) beside the `ui/PaginationConfig:pageSize` row. `17` is the only key that can authorise anything: `CURRENT_MAJOR` is `parseInt(SPEC_VERSION)` with `@objectstack/spec` at 17.7.0, and the ratchet's rule 4 is that only the current major authorises. `authorable-defaults/ui.json` moves exactly one line (`= false` → `= true`), matching both fingerprints. Held.
- **The D3 entry `list-view-edit-inline-default-on`.** One file, `entries/semantic/18.list-view-edit-inline-default-on.ts`, protocol 18 — the same step as `view-pagination-page-size-default-50`. `surface` names the OMITTED key on both carriers of the one schema (a list view's `userActions`, a page's `interfaceConfig.userActions`) and carries no backtick, as the build-upgrade-guide note demands; `replacement` is "nothing" plus the opt-out; `reason` quotes the ruling and says why no D2 exists (a pass writing `false` everywhere would preserve the old posture and defeat the ruling); `acceptanceCriteria` matches the card's acceptance. No tombstone, no `RETIRED_KEYS_BY_MAJOR` row, no D2 — right, nothing is removed. The `registry.ts` hunk is the entry byte-for-byte inside `step18`. Held. One observation, not a finding: the `reason` string carries `objectui#5144`; 12 of the 414 semantic entries on `origin/main` already carry an `objectui#N` in prose, so it is precedented, and `check:doc-authoring` rule 2 scans a different surface.
- **Regenerated references.** Four rows — `view.mdx` ×3, `page.mdx` ×1 — now read `optional (default: \`true\`)` with the new describe. At head, `git grep` for the old describe text ("Off by default: the list") hits only this PR's own changeset quoting it; no rendered row survives. `TypeScript Type Check` (the job that runs every spec artifact gate, `check:docs` and `check:authorable-surface` included) concluded `success` on this head, which is the CI reading that the JSON-schema and docs artifacts are current.
- **Accept set unchanged, only the parsed default moves.** `editInline` stays `z.boolean()`; `.default()` alone moves; the inferred type is `boolean` on both sides, which is why `check:api-surface` has nothing to say. The five pins hold the contract: absent parses to `true` on the schema and through `ListViewSchema`; explicit `false` and `true` keep their values; the view-level `inlineEdit: true` still parses with no `userActions` block materialised (the fold is the renderer's). The dev's ablation (`.default(false)` back) reads as exactly the two default pins red, blob-equal restore — consistent with the diff; not re-run here.
- **Every other place that still states the old default**, at head: `.changeset/console-20c6d351ad74.md` lines 24 and 71 say the console at pin `20c6d351ad74` reads an absent key with the spec's default, off — true of that build until objectui#12086 lands and the pin moves; carrier named in ③. Root `CHANGELOG.md:1677` is release-owned history and stays. `content/docs/ui/views.mdx:111` lists the view-level `inlineEdit` with no default; `layout-dsl.mdx:667` is `record:details`' own `inlineEdit`, a different key; `object.zod.ts:2043` says only that `editInline` is a view key. No example and no `skills/**` file in this repository states the old default; no in-repo metadata declares `editInline` at all. The permission gate and objectui are untouched, as the card requires.

### ② Semver level

- **`minor` is right; `major` is not, even though pre mode would admit it.** `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` ships breaking changes as `minor` for the launch window (end condition: GA, not reached); its RC exemption lets a `major` through while `.changeset/pre.json` reads `mode: pre`, tag `next`, so `major` was available — but the repository's own default-flip precedents on this line all took `minor`: `view-pagination-page-size-default-50` (`8ecbe0f`, under `### Minor Changes`), `approval-escalation-enabled-default-flip` ("shipped as `minor` under the repo's launch-window convention"), `audience-posture-default-invite-only` (same words). Protocol 12's `rest-requireauth-default-flip` (`7c09621`) sits under `### Major Changes`, but that was before the window and is not the rule now. The fixed group already carries the pending `major` that opens the v18 line (`22080-v18-line-opens.md`, `22130-protocol-18.md`), so this `minor` moves no version and rides the `18.0.0-next.N` train. The BREAKING banner is present and is the only breaking signal the ADR-0087 gate reads here (no `major`, no bang on the changeset's first line, no `narrowing` arm); the marker `registered list-view-edit-inline-default-on` resolves at head and is new in this diff; the FROM → TO table and the one-line fix are there. Held.
- **The `Clause-②` arm is NOT right, and this is the one finding of record.** The line answers 「本卡放宽接受集或扩大公开面吗」, and the ruled definition (`pr-automation.yml` WHICH LEVEL, the maintainer's ruling on #15294) is "a purely additive widening of a published package's public surface (a new exported symbol on an `index`, a new accepted key or value)". This diff adds no export, no key and no value; the changeset itself says "The accept set is unchanged" and declares the act BREAKING, and the ADR-0087 gate's own docblock says "A widening is not a break". One act cannot be a purely additive widening and a break at once. A moved default is neither a widening nor a narrowing of the accept set, so the truthful declaration is `Clause-②: no` with no arm, breaking-ness carried where the window puts it — the banner and the marker. The card's parenthetical ("a view declaring nothing gains an affordance it did not have") reads the console's behaviour, not the package's surface. Origin: the card and the dispatch claim `6094254055`; the dev copied the line as `os-dev.md` requires (照抄, ⛔ 不自造), so the correction is the seat's — on the claim, then on the PR body (line 2) and `.changeset/22605-spec-list-view-edit-inline-default-on.md:13`. It matters because the line ships verbatim into `packages/spec/CHANGELOG.md` (416 `Clause-②` lines there today) and is what every later census reads. No gate moves on the correction: the level axis reads `no` as `not-declared` and exits 0 with `minor` untouched; the ADR-0087 gate still reads BREAKING from the banner and still finds the marker. The pm-dispatch instrument-discipline reference assigns the direction to this review (Clause-② 的方向由达档复核裁), so it is ruled here: `no`.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Dev deviations, each answered.** `spec-changes.json` and the upgrade guide reverted to base: right — since #22449 B′ the PR-stage `check:spec-changes` / `check:upgrade-guide` project the registry in memory, and `origin/main` has made the guide a pointer stub; the entries README and the AGENTS.md regenerate table still say otherwise, which is the dev's first `out_of_scope_findings` entry — carrier #22485, named in the ACCEPT, answered. `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, `check:dts-closure`, `check:published-readme-exports` NOT MEASURED locally: CI owns them — `Build Core` is `success` on this head, `Lint & Repo Gates` still running, named below. Seven pushes: AGENTS.md demands a WIP push before every minutes-long step; not a deviation. No re-merge after `main` moved: `origin/main` is now `ad1495796e`, four commits past this PR's merge-base (plugin-audit, plugin-approvals ×2, metadata-protocol), none touching a path of this diff; the queue rebuilds onto current `main`. Model-free commit trailers: what the pre-push hook requires; not a deviation. `test:repo` beyond three files declared to CI: `Test Core` still running, named below.
- **`out_of_scope_findings`, both answered.** (1) README / AGENTS.md regenerate instruction drift → #22485, as above. (2) The console pin changeset's item (4) states the spec default as `false`: accurate about the console at that pin, and the next pin bump's changeset is where the new reading belongs — the carrier the ACCEPT names. Note for that bump: until the pin moves past objectui#12086, this changeset and the console one ship in one train reading "spec default `true`" beside "the console reads the spec's default, off"; each is true of its own artefact, so the pin-bump changeset must say which build it describes.
- **Landing order — escalated, not corrected.** PR #22630 (the skill paragraph, Tier H) is already in the merge queue: `refs/heads/gh-readonly-queue/main/pr-22630-…`, third behind #22623 and #22626, after two APPROVED reviews on its head by `os-zhuang` (in `GOVERNED_APPROVERS`), then `ready_for_review`, `auto_merge_enabled` and `added_to_merge_queue` by that same account — the maintainer's hand, within Tier H's allowance, and no seat act is measured to dequeue it. That reverses the seat's stated order (ACCEPT `6094884470` and the final 速读 on #22630: PR 2 waits for PR 1). The consequence is real and customer-reaching: between the two landings `skills/objectstack-ui/rules/list-views.md` on `main` teaches "on by default" while `view.zod.ts:1535` on `main` still reads `.default(false)` and `@objectstack/spec@latest` is 17.7.0, and the published catalog is installed straight from the repository (`npx skills add objectstack-ai/objectstack/skills`, `npm create objectstack`), not from a release. The seat asks the maintainer whether to hold #22630 (hand removal from the queue) or to accept the window — and either way enqueues this PR's corrected head the moment its re-review PASSes and the two pending contexts are green, so the window is hours, not days.
- **CI on this head at the time of writing.** Required: `Build Core`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `TypeScript Type Check` all `success`; `Lint & Repo Gates` `in_progress`; `Test Core` not yet concluded (shard 4/6 running). No advisory red.
- **Re-review scope.** Every section above except the arm is held. A head that differs from `24d9bdcbf0` only in the two declaration lines (PR body line 2, changeset line 13) re-reviews against this record's ① and ③ unchanged; nothing in `packages/spec/src/**`, the ledgers or the generated pages is asked to move.
